en.note: Personal project, summer 2025. Exhibits 3 and 5 come from one instrumented run of the tool against juejin.cn on 11 October 2026, driven by the tool's own crawler class: counts and timings were recorded, page content was not kept.

stats.label: Ways to locate
stats.hint: XPath, CSS, ID, class, tag · 8 regex patterns

stats.label: Run: pages extracted
stats.hint: title and body on every page · 4.6 min

fig1.title: What one run does, step by step
fig1.caption: Exhibit 1. The loop in the middle is the whole trick: count what the page has loaded, scroll to the bottom, pause, count again, and stop when the target is met, when three rounds add nothing, or after 20 scrolls. Everything after it is ordinary extraction, one page at a time.

nodes.num: to the bottom · 1 s pause · stop after 3 idle rounds or 20

nodes.num: Excel · CSV · MySQL table it creates

fig2.title: The tool running: the same crawl, recorded
fig2.sub: Streamlit UI · 40 articles from juejin.cn · real time for the first seconds, then sped up · ends on the results table
fig2.caption: Exhibit 2. Target URL, item count and the locators go in at the top; the log below shows each scroll round and what it added, then each article page as it is visited, and the run ends on a table with a title, body, images and the custom fields per row, ready to download or write to MySQL.
fig2.alt: Screen recording of the crawler app: the form is filled in, the crawl starts, progress lines appear for scrolling and for each article, and a results table appears at the end

fig3.title: One run on juejin.cn: what each scroll round loaded
fig3.sub: bars = article links on the page when the round started · dots = links collected by the end of it · x = seconds since the page opened · target 60
fig3.caption: Exhibit 3. The home page opened with 29 article links. The first scroll added nothing, the next two added 17 each, and the fourth round crossed the 60-link target 10 seconds in. Collection then switched to visiting the 60 pages one by one, which took the remaining four and a half minutes of the run.

fig4.title: What the tool can be pointed at
fig4.caption: Exhibit 4. Five exact locators plus eight regular expressions cover most list pages; custom fields reuse the same locators, so a run can add author, date and view count without code. Storage infers the MySQL column types from the values it sees.

groups.name: Search
items: Regex over stored HTML: URL · phone · email · image · name

groups.name: Session

fig5.title: The table this run would create
fig5.sub: column types inferred from the 60 extracted rows · fill = share of rows with a value
fig5.caption: Exhibit 5. Titles and bodies were found on every page; the three custom fields were filled on 93% of pages and images on 75%. The body column is LONGTEXT because the median article ran 3,760 characters and the longest 22,332; everything short became VARCHAR(500).

fig2.caption: 图 2。顶部填目标网址、条数和定位方式；下方日志先显示每轮滚动和新增的条数，再显示逐篇访问的进度，最后出现一张每行带标题、正文、图片和自定义字段的结果表，可直接下载或写入 MySQL。

fig3.title: 在掘金上跑一次：每轮滚动加载了多少
fig3.sub: 柱 = 本轮开始时页面上的文章链接数 · 圆点 = 本轮结束时已收集的链接数 · 横轴 = 页面打开后的秒数 · 目标 60
fig3.caption: 图 3。首页打开时有 29 条文章链接。第一次滚动没有新增，接下来两轮各加 17 条，第四轮在第 10 秒越过 60 条的目标。随后切换为逐一访问这 60 个页面，占掉了整次运行剩下的四分半钟。

fig4.title: 这个工具能对准什么
fig4.sub: 定位 → 提取 → 存储，按实际实现列出
fig4.caption: 图 4。五种精确定位加八种正则覆盖大多数列表页；自定义字段复用同一套定位方式，所以不改代码就能多抓作者、日期、阅读数。写库时按看到的值推断 MySQL 列类型。
